argument: PAC and VC theory bound generalization error using sample size, hypothesis-class capacity, confidence, and empirical fit. A schematic bound has form $R(h)\lesssim \hat R(h)+O(\!\sqrt{(C+\log(1/\delta))/n})$, though modern overparameterized systems require data-dependent notions such as margin, norm, stability, or compression.
boundary: Worst-case bounds can be numerically loose.
Parameter count alone is not an adequate capacity measure for modern networks.
IID assumptions and fixed hypothesis classes may fail under adaptive data collection.

title: Generalization Depends on Capacity Relative to Data and Margin

argument: For a fixed training or inference budget, performance depends on how capacity, data quantity and quality, optimization steps, precision, and deployment cost are allocated. Increasing one dimension while starving another can waste compute or induce overfitting.
boundary: Optimal allocation is workload- and hardware-dependent.
Capabilities and risks do not necessarily scale smoothly with loss.

interpretation: Principia should store the budget definition behind an efficiency claim. Token count, FLOPs, latency, energy, memory, and monetary cost are not interchangeable.
